evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said 'the next step would be to put together an estimate so I'm going to be asking you some questions about your move would take about maybe seven to ten minutes and then you can walk away with a quote you can depend on' — time-boxed and promise present, but rep did not wait for customer to say yes before launching into discovery; moved directly into 'what's your last name again' without a clear confirmation pause.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked 'Other than the price obviously. What are your biggest concerns about the move-in any questions do you want answers to on this call?' — properly asked before logistics probing, and customer replied 'No ma'am.' Full N/A credit awarded for Two Layers Deep and Active Listening Reflection because no concerns were raised.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep gathered property type (storage unit), floor (first floor), indoor/outdoor (indoor), special items (TV, washer/dryer), box count (~10-15), and drop-off property type (house) and stories (one). Missing: walking distance, additional rooms at destination, and complete detail on the destination property layout. Partial credit.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asked 'approximately how many boxes in, in the storage unit' and customer answered 'Probably 10:00 to fifteen.' No follow-up on overflow or typical count framing.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep did not ask 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' Customer stated items were already boxed and ready ('everything's box and ready. We don't need to like box anything up'), but the rep never proactively offered the service.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provided hourly rate ($192 for two movers) and mentioned 2.5-hour minimum, but did not anchor to a typical range for this move size or personalize the estimate to customer's specific situation (storage unit clearance, two units, etc.). Partial credit.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed trip fee ($280) upfront, explained hourly rate covers supplies/gas/taxes/insurance, stated no hidden fees, no credit card fee, no reassembly fees, and mentioned 2.5-hour minimum. Full framing present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or any equivalent. Customer interrupted mid-pricing explanation ('I don't mind heard me cut you off. I just don't. Once you got to go through based on your rates that's a, that's more than what I'm gonna pay right now') and declined before the rep could close the estimate section. Not asked.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated 'when you book your move with us, we'll lock in a firm arrival window for you. If we're late, $50 comes off immediately and after the first hour it's an extra $25 for every fifteen minutes after that.' Full delivery of discount terms.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated 'we have our no worries, damage coverage. So, up to $2,000 included in the hourly rate and we pay it out in four to six days.' Delivered fully — coverage amount, no-deductible framing (included, not add-on), and payment timeline.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent after delivering the Two Promises. No loop closure attempted.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine version. Call ended abruptly after customer declined on price.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any explicit close. Customer cut off the call by declining the price before any ask could be made.

top_strength: Rep effectively gathered all four discovery basics (name, move date, pickup/dropoff zip codes, home size) early and asked the genuine agenda question before starting logistics probing, showing adherence to Section 1–2 structure.
coaching_note: Rep must pause and confirm 'does that sound good?' after the quid pro quo framing in Section 1, and must ask 'Does that feel fair?' after presenting the estimate in Section 4 — both are load-bearing moments where silence discipline prevents objection-stacking and gives the customer room to accept or surface concerns before pricing discussion ends.
